newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela congress will approve ARCO oil project.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela congress will approve ARCO oil project.

text.p: Venezuela's Congress will approve a $3.5 billion heavy oil joint-venture between state oil subsidiary Corpoven and Atlantic Richfield Co before March 2, a congress leader said on Thursday.
Virgilio Avila Vivas, president of the Senate Energy and Mines Committee, said it would be approved before the end of the current extraordinary session of Congress on March 2.

The joint-venture aims to produce 197,000 barrels per day (bpd) of heavy crude from the Hamaca province of the Orinoco Tar Belt and convert it into 181,000 bpd of 25 degrees API crude. Corpoven and ARCO each have a 30 percent share in the scheme, while Texaco and Phillips each have 20 percent.

Corpoven president Guillermo Archila said there were various other companies interested in participating in the Orinoco Tar Belt, but would not confirm rumours that Corpoven was talking to Amerada Hess about such a scheme.
"We are always studying other opportunities, but at the moment we have not signed any others," he told reporters after the committee hearing.
He confirmed that Corpoven has agreed to do a study with Exxon in the same area.
